evidence.description: The declared independent-unit column is accession_id, and the CSV contains exactly 16 data rows with 16 distinct accession IDs (FSB-101 through FSB-116); no ID appears on more than one row.
The workflow explicitly guards against repeated independent-unit entry: it aborts if any accession_id occurs on more than one row before any statistics are computed.
evidence.observed_value: SystemExit raised on duplicate accession codes

evidence.description: The selected statistical procedure is a paired t-test on one within-row difference per accession, so the number of analysed observations (16) equals the number of independent units, and the reported degrees of freedom equal n - 1 = 15.

evidence.description: Recomputation from the raw CSV confirms the reported selected result: the 16 within-accession differences (cryo minus freezer) are 4, 12, 1, 18, 7, 2, 10, 1, 16, 5, 8, 19, 1, 9, 4, 11, giving mean 8.00 pp, SD 6.00, SE 1.50, t = 8.00/1.50 = 5.333 on 15 df, 95% CI 4.80 to 11.20 pp, and Wilcoxon W = 0 since every difference is positive. All match the report, so the reported statistics correspond to exactly one entry per independent unit.

[selected-result] Paired t-test on 16 accession-level differences (one difference per accession): cryogenic storage at -196 C raised 18-month spore germination by 8.00 percentage points relative to -20 C storage (95% CI 4.80 to 11.20 pp; t(15) = 5.333, p < 0.0001, two-sided).

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I tried to establish the issue by (1) scanning all 16 CSV rows for any repeated accession_id value (none found; 16 unique IDs), (2) checking whether the workflow expands, duplicates, or pools rows before testing so that one accession could enter the test more than once (it does not: it reads rows once, computes one difference per row, and passes exactly those arrays to stats.ttest_rel and stats.wilcoxon), (3) checking whether reported sample size or degrees of freedom exceed the number of independent units, which would betray hidden repeated entries (n = 16 and df = 15 match 16 units exactly), and (4) recomputing the mean difference, SD, SE, t statistic, CI, and Wilcoxon statistic from the raw data, all of which reproduce the reported values under one entry per accession. I also considered whether spores_scored = 100 per plate constitutes repeated unit entry, but individual spores are never entered as rows; only the accession-level percentage is analysed. No path to demonstrating the issue class survived these checks.
